name: Kansas

sales.rateNote: State retailers' sales tax of 6.5% (K.S.A. 79-3603); since January 1, 2025, 18% of it goes to the state highway fund. The state rate on food and food ingredients is 0% since January 1, 2025 (K.S.A. 79-3603d). Cities and counties add local sales taxes.

local.levies: city retailers' sales taxes (general and special purpose) and countywide retailers' sales taxes, administered and collected by the state
local.capNote: K.S.A. 12-189: a city rate may not exceed 2% for general purposes plus 1% for special purposes (special-purpose city taxes expire after 10 years); a countywide rate may not exceed 1%, with statutory exceptions allowing 1.25% to 2% or more in named counties.

groceries.note: The state rate on food and food ingredients fell from 6.5% to 4% on January 1, 2023, 2% on January 1, 2024 and 0% on January 1, 2025. Prepared food stays taxable, except bakery items, unheated food sold by weight or volume and food needing further cooking when sold without utensils. The state 0% rate does not by itself remove local sales taxes.

clothing.note: No clothing exemption; clothing is tangible personal property taxed at 6.5% plus local tax.

otherRates.item: residential gas, electricity, heat and heating fuels (propane, LP gas, coal, wood)
otherRates.note: State rate 0% for noncommercial residential use and agricultural use.

otherRates.item: sales within a redevelopment district established under K.S.A. 74-8921
otherRates.note: Additional 2% tax until the district's bonds are paid.

sales.holidayNote: Kansas has no sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: Compensating use tax of 6.5% on items used, stored or consumed in Kansas without Kansas sales tax (K.S.A. 79-3703).

facts.text: Kansas phased its state grocery tax down from 6.5% to 4% (2023), 2% (2024) and 0% on January 1, 2025.
Bread, bagels, cakes, cookies and other bakery items count as groceries at 0% when sold without eating utensils.
A city can levy up to 2% general plus 1% special-purpose sales tax, and special-purpose taxes expire after 10 years.
Since January 1, 2025, 18% of the state sales tax is dedicated to the state highway fund.
Home heating (residential gas, electricity, propane, wood) is exempt from the state sales tax.

property.levied: counties, cities, townships, school districts (including the statewide school levy under K.S.A. 72-5142) and special districts

assessment.text: Assessed value is a percentage of appraised value set by class: residential real property 11.5%; commercial and industrial real property 25%; agricultural land 30% of its use value; vacant lots 12%; other real property 30%.

homestead.name: Residential exemption from the statewide school levy
homestead.text: Since tax year 2024, the first $75,000 of appraised value of residential property is exempt from the statewide school levy (K.S.A. 72-5142); local levies still apply to the full value.

facts.text: Kansas homes are assessed at 11.5% of appraised value, versus 25% for commercial and industrial property.
The first $75,000 of a home's appraised value has been exempt from the statewide school levy since tax year 2024 (2024 special session law).
Farmland is taxed on its agricultural use value, not its market value.
